_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band1_lower_meadows. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 1000-1999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

props._why: the cluster's anchor -- an anvil mounted on its own stump
faces the anvil across the nook -- pulled in 0.7m (round 1 blind critic: the anvil/whetstone and crate/workbench read as two separate groups, not one station)
a sharpening stone within reach of the bench -- pulled in 0.4m, same reason
stock crate behind the anvil -- pulled in 0.9m, same reason
a tool left leaning, mid-repair -- pulled in 0.3m, same reason
the cluster's anchor -- overflow from the last harvest

set right against the barrel's side, not just nearby -- round 2 blind critic: a loose arc of props near a wall reads as dumped, not a task. This is meant to read as one pile: a load just carried out and set down together.

touching the barrel's other side, tipped at an angle rather than square -- just set down, not arranged. FarmCrate_Carrot swapped out earlier (round 1 blind critic): its vertex-colour-tinted contents render as an unreadable white/grey smear, a model defect not a placement one.
in front of the pile, facing back toward it -- the tool that did the carrying, set down after
the big piece of the same load, closing the pile from the front

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor -- a travelling trainer's pack, dropped beside the practice-meadow path, kept as its own separate stop rather than crammed against the supply pile (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'reads as three container props at even spacing... scatter-list output, not a place'). Sited off route 2 ([18,-24]->[30,-40], terrain_playground.json), inside the practice-meadow clearing (vegetation.json, centre [30,-40] r16) but well short of the arena itself.

EV7-clusters-fix: the pile's anchor. This meadow slopes here for real -- a corner-height probe against the crate's own exact footprint (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd) measures 0.137-0.172m of spread across the headings tried, barely moved by yaw alone (165deg: 0.137m vs the old -25deg heading's 0.145m -- yaw was never going to fix this on its own). `sink_m` 0.08 is what actually settles it: added to the model's own ~0.05m embed, the crate's rigid bottom sits ~0.13m below the sampled centre height, which is deeper than half this footprint's worst-case corner spread, so every corner ends up buried in the terrain mesh rather than floating above it, regardless of which way it's turned. `Bench` (a trestle table) is DROPPED entirely -- the critic's own offered alternative ('drop the table and commit to a supply cache at a waypoint composition'): props.gd places every prop flush to the ground with no way to rest one ON another, so the table's flat top could never actually hold the crate/sack/barrel it was meant to -- they always passed clean through its legs. A cache of things set down together, not a furnished stop, is what this system can honestly build.

EV7-clusters-fix: touching the crate's side (0.83m centre-to-centre, matching the two footprints' combined radius) so the pair reads as one pile someone set down together, not a scatter -- distinct spacing from the pack 1.9m away, breaking the old even 3-way spacing the critic named as 'placed by script.' Still the plain supply barrel, not the farmhouse's apple-branded one.

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor, moved to hug the footbridge's own west landing (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd -- bridge local frame x=-5.3, z=1.4, just outside the deck/rail collider's z=+/-1.05 half-extent and past the stone abutment tile at local x=-3.9..-5.9) instead of sitting marooned in open lawn ~3m further out (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'marooned ~6m from the house and ~4m off the bridge head in open lawn'). `sink_m` buries the crate's own shallow 0.05m embed a little further so grass doesn't show lit up under its skirt -- this spot is flat (0.000-0.006m corner spread, real terrain data, not sloped), so the old 'floating crate' complaint here was the shallow embed, not a slope.

EV7-clusters-fix: actually leaning against the crate's near face now, not standing bolt upright ('the axe LEVITATES: bolt upright, unsupported, haft ending mid-air'). This model is authored vertical in its own glTF (a baked -90deg node rotation puts its long axis on Y regardless of yaw -- confirmed with tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd, not guessed), so no yaw value could ever lay it down; `pitch_deg` is new on scripts/world/props.gd for exactly this. Anchor and pitch picked from the same probe's world-space AABB check so the tilted mesh's low end sits in the grass and its body actually overlaps the crate's east face (~0.05m real contact, not just visually adjacent), clear of the crate's own footprint so it doesn't clip through a corner.

EV7-clusters-fix: moved to the crate's own east/bridge-facing side, in front rather than tucked behind it ('the rope coil -- the most purpose-carrying prop -- is 90% hidden behind the crate'). This is the side a player sees first walking off the bridge, so the repair stock reads immediately instead of needing to walk around the crate to find it.

EV7-clusters-fix: water bucket at the pile's far (west) side, foot of the pile -- kept off the deck/rail collider the same way the rest of the cluster is now (local z 1.75, not 0.89 like the position this replaced, which was inside the walkway's own collider footprint).

set against the woodpile's own foot (0.86m centre to centre, touching), not floating separately -- one pile, not a scatter.

the inn's cellar barrels, south of its east door (door node (3.5,-9); east wall collider ends at x 3.73, so 0.9m clear), on the square side where the well-to-inn path arrives. A public house's clutter, not a private home's.

clusters._why_vp5: VP5 (visual-parity village lane), 2026-09-02. Two blind judges (ralph/reports/visual-parity/VP0-baseline/JUDGE-village-pond.md, ralph/reports/audit/E-locations/JUDGE-AUDIT-E-locations-2026-08-31.md) read this ground as 'a plain open meadow ... no arena, ring, stands, or banner'. The geography fixes what a ring can be: the corridor spine (terrain_playground.json trail.bands[0], (27.5,-16)->(14,20)) runs straight through the field 4m west of the board, the three tournament trainers stand at (20,12) (band1 trainers.json) with an 11m combat arena (combat_arena.gd) around the fight, and the village fence runs 3.3m behind the board. So the ring is the road's east verge, bounded by the fence: the EVENT read comes from the key art's own settlement device -- green banners on posts (quaternius_castle `Banner`, retinted to the board's banner green, never Team Tether's oxblood) -- two of them flanking the road where it enters the ground, one on the ring's west side; the two spectator benches re-sited to face the ring from outside the trainers' axis (E1's east bench stood 0.4m from Halda, on top of her); and a small staging pile (crate, bucket, bag) by the board for the team waiting its turn, with a barrel by the east bench. Everything solid sits >= 7m from the arena centre (20,10) except the board-side staging pile, 4.5m off its axis. Positions checked against the built scene (board node (20,15) yaw -155, Halda (23.5,11.5), Bryn (13,9), the berry node (28,6), the trail road's actual line, and the NEW boundary edge (30,11)->(15.98,22.59), which is 2.5-4m from the pile and the west bench).

clusters.name: trail_camp

rest._why:
T5-CADENCE, closing T4-REGIONS' third-ranked chapter gap (ralph/reports/REGION_AUDIT_2026-08-30.md: 'Camps are set dressing'). This is the best-dressed camp in the game -- 18 props, a bed, a lit bonfire, a bench and a stool -- and it is a named map landmark (`band1_trail_camp`), and until this block it could not be used for anything. The audit's exit-criterion verdict for band 1's camp/recovery row was FAIL, with the reason written as 'a map landmark that promises rest and delivers scenery'. `scripts/world/rest_point.gd` is what reads this; the offer it stands up is the SAME one the player-built Camp makes, not a better one.

SITED at the fire, 1.6m east of it, because the fire is what makes this read as a camp from the trail and because that is exactly where `camp.gd` hangs its own rest prompt relative to its own fire. The fire ring is ~2.1m across (campfire_stone_ring at scale 1.05), so 1.6m clears the stones.
rest.label: Rest until morning

creature_bed._why:
The camp's own creature bed, and the half of this that makes 'recovery' mean anything 900m from home: `game_state.gd::_tick_creature_bed_recovery()` heals an occupant gradually whether or not the player is standing here, so a creature bedded down at the trail camp is genuinely unavailable and genuinely recovering -- exit criterion H3.

ADDED rather than converted. The `camp_bed` prop already in this cluster stays exactly where it is, inside the tent's mouth, as the TRAINER's own sleeping surface; a trail camp a trainer keeps has a place for the team as well as for the person, and that is one more instance of an already-installed mesh rather than a new asset. Sited south-east of the fire in the one genuinely open quarter of the camp: 3.2m from the fire, 2.8m from the firewood log, 2.3m from the tall-grass tuft, and clear of the tent/bed footprint on the opposite side. Yaw turns its long axis toward the fire the way the bench and stool already face it. VISUAL NOTE: sited from the measured prop layout, not from a frame -- worth a look when this camp is next captured.

props._why: REVERTED to round 3's Bonfire_Fire + ignite() after two rounds of dedicated Meshy generation (camp_firewood, camp_flame -- text-to-3D, retextured, non-uniform-scaled, repositioned) each failed an independent Fable review against the reference: the log pile read as flat slabs or a rock cairn rather than logs, and the flame read as an opaque carved spire with no emissive light cast on its surroundings, in both attempts. This combination was never itself criticised by either review -- both were reviewing the NEW pieces specifically -- and it is round 3's own solved problem: `Bonfire_Fire.obj`'s three-surface OBJ import (Wood/LightWood/Fire) with `ignite()` lighting the real `Fire` surface, plus `campfire_glow.gd`'s light/embers/smoke overlay including its billboard halo (default `include_halo=true`, unlike the generated flame's own `flame_mesh` path). Owner directive to wrap up rather than keep spending Meshy rounds on a shape that was not converging; `camp_firewood.glb`/`camp_flame.glb` stay committed under assets/props/generated_camp/ for a future attempt, just not wired into this cluster.

Replaces round 3's six hand-placed Rock_Medium instances with one Meshy-generated ring mesh, textured to match the reference board's own fire-ring stones. Raw 2.00m diameter; 0.85 gives ~1.7m, the same footprint the six-stone version measured at (0.82-0.94m radius). The fire and its glow overlay sit inside the ring's own empty centre, which is why this prop carries no `glow` key of its own -- the flame is the Bonfire above, not this. Sourced via Meshy image-to-3D from an owner-supplied reference board (docs/art/reference/owner-board-2026-08-23-camp-set.png, docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) -- an explicit owner directive and reference art, which is the actual prerequisite CLAUDE.md's Meshy-generation rule enforces; that board's own bed panel carried another game's paw-print/leaf emblem and both were removed from the crops before submission plus banned in the negative prompt (tools/art_pipeline/meshy.py NEGATIVE_CAMP_BED) before generation, not after. ROUND 3: a dispatched Fable fidelity review against the reference found the stones individually too small/flat and too gapped relative to the reference's tightly packed boulders -- a defect internal to this single rigid mesh that scale cannot fully fix (relative gaps and per-stone height-to-footprint ratio are baked into the geometry), but a straight size increase at least makes each stone read chunkier. Scale raised 0.85 -> 1.05, ~1.7m -> ~2.1m diameter -- the only lever available without a further regeneration, which Fable rated this piece as not clearly needing (the tent did).
Long seat facing the fire across it, tangential yaw so its 2.78m length runs perpendicular to the radius. Unchanged from round 3.

A third, informal seat. Round 3's environment/nature log_large was found this round to render with an untextured near-white placeholder material -- the independent blind critic's unidentifiable 'pale rectangular chute object' -- and was replaced with Kenney's real textured tree-log.glb, CC0, already vendored for scripts/build/camp.gd's own fire.
A second, smaller seat on the fire's opposite side from the bench. Unchanged from round 3.
Firewood, radial not tangential (the opposite rule from the two seats, for the opposite reason). Same environment/nature defect as log_large above; same Kenney replacement.
Supply crate, behind the seats rather than between them and the fire. Unchanged from round 3.
Leaning against the crate. Unchanged from round 3.
Coiled beside the crate/bag pile. Unchanged from round 3.
Measured raw 3.34 x 3.12 x 1.75m with its origin 1.46m above its own base; 0.18 with sink_m -0.25 lifts it back to ground level. Unchanged from round 3.
Water barrel, already the right size at scale 1.0 (measured 0.70 x 0.90 x 0.70m). Unchanged from round 3.

Owner's pick from the eight-candidate contact sheet: round 1's multi-image-to-3D result. Sourced via Meshy image-to-3D from an owner-supplied reference board (docs/art/reference/owner-board-2026-08-23-camp-set.png, docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md). Round 1's geometry (multi-image-to-3D, three reference crops, refine tier) is the version the owner chose after reviewing a contact sheet of all eight candidates generated across rounds 1-5 -- rounds 2-3 tried to fix its proportions via image reference changes and converged on the same shape (images dominate text in this pipeline); round 4-5 tried text-to-3D instead and traded the proportion problem for a construction-fidelity problem (a teepee, then missing patches/rigging/weathering once corrected to an A-frame). Kept round 1: weathered patched canvas, crossed lashed pole tips at both ends, matches the reference board's own material and stitching most closely of any candidate even though its proportions read flatter than the reference.

Replaces round 3b's ground bedroll with a proper raised camp bed -- lashed log frame, stuffed mattress, pillow -- matching the board's own PAL BED panel far more closely than a flat bedroll ever could. Raw 1.23 x 0.41 x 1.90m needs no scaling. Laid inside the tent's mouth, its long axis parallel to the tent's ridge, head end under the canvas. Sourced via Meshy image-to-3D from an owner-supplied reference board (docs/art/reference/owner-board-2026-08-23-camp-set.png, docs/specs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) -- an explicit owner directive and reference art, which is the actual prerequisite CLAUDE.md's Meshy-generation rule enforces; that board's own bed panel carried another game's paw-print/leaf emblem and both were removed from the crops before submission plus banned in the negative prompt (tools/art_pipeline/meshy.py NEGATIVE_CAMP_BED) before generation, not after.
Authored scenery, breaking the clearing's own edge. Unchanged from round 3.
Second bush, west edge. Unchanged from round 3.
Low fern, different silhouette from the bushes. Unchanged from round 3.
Tall grass tuft, trail-side foreground. Unchanged from round 3.
Low clover clump, moved slightly from round 3's position to stay clear of the relocated tent/bed pair's footprint.

clusters._why: BAND1-D1-v3. Relocated from (348,919) to (344,935). The old site drops 1.2m across the camp's own 7m footprint (tools/_probe_camp_ground.gd), which is why round 2's props sat at nine different heights and why the wide frame read as a grass slope with objects on it. tools/_probe_camp_flat.gd swept the ground 5-14m off the loop trail and (344,935) is the flattest shelf near it. Round 5 (blind-critic follow-up + owner-directed Meshy generation) swapped the fire ring, tent and bed for owner-referenced generated assets and fixed the environment/nature untextured-material defect the critic's 'unidentifiable pale rectangular object' finding traced back to (log_large).

clusters.name: old_champion_rest
clusters._why: Prompt 30 asks every optional activity for 'local environmental storytelling so it belongs to its region'. Old Bram sitting alone in an empty field is a man standing in a field; a man sitting on a fallen tree he has clearly sat on for years, with a ring of old stones and his gear beside him, is somebody who comes here. Seven props, deliberately few: this is a place a person uses, not a settlement. Every model is one this band's trail_camp already uses, so no new prop family enters the chapter for one NPC (CLAUDE.md's one-prop-family rule).

props._why: The seat. He is placed facing 215 degrees, which is across it and back toward the road he is watching -- a man who sits where he can see who is coming. environment/nature's log_large is one of only two models in that pack that render correctly through props.gd (see the trail_camp entries and ralph/BLOCKED.md for why the rest do not); this is one of them.

First of three stones set in a loose arc in front of the log -- the fire he does not light any more. Same models and the same 0.11-0.22 scale band as trail_camp's fire ring, for the same measured reason: the RockPath family are flat pebble mosaics and read as gravel at any scale.
Second stone.
Third stone, the smallest, closing the arc.
His bag, set down at the far end of the log rather than carried -- the difference between somebody passing through and somebody who has been here since morning.
Authored edge on the approach side, so the 13m clearing his arena needs does not read as a bald circle in open grass. Same lesson trail_camp learned the hard way.
Second piece of authored edge, opposite side, at a different height so the two do not read as a pair.

clusters.name: tether_waypost
clusters._why: T3-BRIDGE, owner-direction §5: 'Team Tether patrol or evidence' as its own checklist item, distinct from the wilds/trainers/resources already authored here and distinct from the south_bridge_grunt fight itself -- everything Team Tether in Band 1 before this was spoken (Oskar/the Foreman/the Ranger's dialogue, data/dialogue/village.json) or fought (the bridge). Nothing physical said it until now. Follows data/config/bands/band3_the_river_lock/props.json order 3000's own established grammar for this exact faction beat (a staked, retinted Banner claims ground) rather than inventing a new one, but stripped down to EVIDENCE per §32's reveal ladder (data/config/old_quarry.json's own _comment_evidence: 'no dialogue in this file, no interactable on the hardware, no note to read' at this stage of the ladder) -- no brazier, no held position, because nobody mans this one. A dropped crate and a staked banner read as 'they were through here, recently, and didn't stay' rather than 'this is a manned post', which is the correct claim for ground the player has not been challenged on yet. Sited on-route (within `tools/_probe_band1_cadence.py`'s own 60m on-route lateral call) at arc~2100m of 2403m -- inside the last kilometre before the south_bridge_grunt checkpoint (arc~2372m), so the escalation reads as: evidence, then the grunt himself. Checked clear of every other authored entry in this band (nearest, the order-1049 mudsnout pocket, is 48m off).

props._why: the anchor -- a supply crate that fell, or was left, off the same road the grunt now watches the end of. Stamped no differently from any other loose crate in the world; it is the banner beside it that says whose.

Same module, same oxblood hex, same scale/pitch/sink_m as the river checkpoint's own staked banner (band3_the_river_lock/props.json order 3000) -- CLAUDE.md's reserved Team Tether accent, no new mesh, no new colour. Yaw and pitch match that entry's own reasoning, not a re-derivation: 2.6 gives the same ~1.8m reading height at the same distance a passing player judges it from, and the small negative pitch/sink_m keep the unmodelled buried pole end from floating. TUNABLE against the actual road bearing here (roughly -72deg by the spine's own (180,1200)-(30,1250) segment) once this can be rendered and checked; 15deg is a legible-to-a-passerby placeholder, not a probed value.

one round not yet split, dropped beside the stack at a different angle so the pile reads as work in progress, not a placed pair.

The open east side of Grandpa's kitchen garden (farm.json plots, now railed on the north and west by village.json): a picking crate and the watering bucket set down where the beds are worked from. 0.9m east of the eastern plot column, 3.5m from Old Perrin's spot at (-15,-5), 3.7m from the deadwood node at (-14,-8).

props._why: the harvest crate, half full.
the watering bucket, touching the crate's side.

clusters.name: grandpa_door_lantern
clusters._why: VP2-NIGHT judge pass, 2026-09-02: '01-village-grandpa-yard-night' (marker stand GrandpaHouse/outside -> GrandpaHouse/door) reads NPCs at the door as 'silhouetted to illegibility (a little warm light near the door)'. `grandpa_house.gd`'s door marker is `to_global(Vector3(INNER_W*0.5+WALL_T+1.2, 0, 0))` = world (-15.7,-16) off `playground_world.gd`'s HOUSE_AT (-22,-16) with no rotation -- the same figure this file's own `village_twins_yard` cluster already cites for its woodpile ('built door node (-15.7,-16), wall extent x -16.05'), not a fresh guess. No lantern/lamp/brazier mesh exists anywhere under assets/ (torch_prop.gd's own header: a find across assets/props and assets/environment for torch/flame/lantern turns up nothing but this same Bonfire), and this lane may only edit config, not scripts, so the reused mechanism is the one already-solved warm-practical-light recipe every camp in the chapter uses (`Bonfire_Fire.obj`'s real `Fire` surface + `ignite()` + `campfire_glow.gd`'s light/ember/smoke overlay, `glow: campfire`) -- scaled far down from every camp's own use of it (band1's trail camp 0.45, band4's patrol posting 0.42) to read as a small dooryard fire-pot rather than a bonfire dropped on the threshold, which is what 'a lantern by a door, not stage lighting' asks for. ONE light only -- no stone ring, no supply pile -- since a fire ring/log cache would read as a camp, not a doorstep. Sited 1.24m from the door node at (-15.4,-17.2): south of the door on the same side as the existing woodpile/crate pair (-15.0,-18.9)/(-14.3,-19.4) so it reads as one dooryard rather than clutter on both flanks, 1.75m clear of the woodpile, 1.63m clear of the 'Grandpa's House' route's own painted-path endpoint (-16.5,-16.0) (terrain_playground.json paths.routes), and off the door-to-outside walking lane (village_twins_yard's own 'x -16..-9.7 at z~-15' figure runs close to z=-16 at this x, not through z=-17.2). Sits in `building_aprons.footprints[0]`'s (centre -22,-16, half_extents 5.3x3.3) feather zone, same as the woodpile/crate beside it -- worked dooryard ground, not raw lawn, the same convention every other VP5 entry in this file already follows.

props._why: The door light itself. `scale` 0.22 -- roughly half band4's already-small 0.42 patrol posting -- keeps the log pile door-side-brazier small rather than reading as a hearth blocking the threshold; `glow_scale` deliberately left at the chapter's own 1.0 default (LIGHT_RANGE 8.0m, LIGHT_BASE_ENERGY 3.4, warm colour (1.0,0.68,0.32) -- campfire_glow.gd's own constants) rather than dimmed further, because the judge's finding was specifically that NPCs at the door are ILLEGIBLE at night: an 8m warm pool centred 1.24m from the door is what actually reads Oskar/Grandpa's faces, and every other camp in the chapter already proves this exact energy/range reads as a warm practical light rather than daylight at night without complaint. `yaw_deg` 35 (not a flat 0/90) so the log pile does not stand squared-off against the wall, matching this file's own 'not one more object than the yard needs, every object placed on purpose' convention for the rest of the dooryard.

Deliberately minimal -- one seat and one fire, not a second trail_camp -- so it reads as a single traveller's stop (the fisher's own) rather than a second authored campsite competing with the band's real rest point 700m south. Sited by a real ground scan of the pond's own shore (tools/_probe_world_content_0903b.gd; the water is at level -17.0 and the straight-line candidate off the road here came back underwater): this point is dry (h=-14.48, 2.52m above the waterline), on the pond's south-east shore, 10m from the fisher NPC (village_npcs.json-pattern placement, data/config/bands/band1_lower_meadows/pond_npc.json) so the two read as one scene, and clear (>=30m) of the bridge_repair_site prop cluster and every wild cluster already authored at the pond.

A small stone ring around the fire, scaled down from the trail camp's own 1.05 (a ~2.1m ring) to match this camp's one-person scale.
The seat, facing the fire across it and out toward the water beyond -- a place to sit and watch a line, which is what the fisher NPC beside this cluster is doing.

clusters.name: bridge_approach_fence
clusters._why: WORLD-CONTENT, docs/specs/BAND1_ROUTE_CONTRACT.md place 5 (the Bridge approach): 'a broken-fence line leading the eye toward the South Bridge on the approach'. Four sections of the settlement's own wooden-fence kit (quaternius_medieval, already vendored -- CLAUDE.md: no new prop family), NOT village.json's structural `fence_run` prefab (that is a sealed boundary line with gate logic; this is scenery, an old field-fence nobody has mended). Run along the road's own shoulder from arc 2170 to arc 2250 of trail.bands[0], 8-10m off the centreline, ending short of the south_bridge_grunt checkpoint (order 1000, arc 2371) so the eye is led TO the gate rather than past it. The third section is toppled (`pitch_deg`) -- the 'broken' the route contract asks for, not just an intact line -- reading as an old field boundary from before Team Tether closed the crossing, left to rot the way the tether_waypost cluster (order 1020) reads as evidence rather than a manned position.

props._why: First section, arc 2170, running with the road's own bearing.
Second section, arc 2190, continuing the line.

Third section, arc 2210 -- the broken one, tipped almost flat (`pitch_deg` 72, the same lean mechanic `bridge_repair_site`'s axe already uses on this prop family's fixed vertical authoring) with its foot sunk into the grass rather than floating.

Fourth section, arc 2230, the road's bend toward the bridge -- the line's last intact panel before the gap the broken section leaves, ending the eye's path at the checkpoint ahead rather than at the fence itself.
